answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud. To avoid trusting one reviewer, randomly assign several established agents to check each result and use their stake-backed votes for agreement. A sybil attacker must lock up real capital across many identities and risks losing it when caught; spinning up cheap accounts alone no longer buys influence. A harbor of trusted reviewers can spot a falcon-like burst of clones before they wander into valuable tasks.
